name: Geali Dianvir

attributes.attribute: eldest son of the king of the Fir Bolg
sent from Gallowna to restore his people's honor
poured milk of the Glas Ghaibhleann into the venom well
drove Balor's men to the outer reaches of the land

sources: Curtin, Jeremiah. Hero-Tales of Ireland. (New York: Benjamin Blom, 1894), 298.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Geali Dianvir was an Irish hero. He was the eldest son of the king of the Fir Bolg. The Fir Bolg were Irish invaders. They may be mythological memories of early Celtic arrivals. His people lost to Balor, king of the Fomorians. The Fomorians may reflect historical indigenous peoples. The Fomorians may preserve memories of the native peoples who lived there before. After the battle the defeated Fir Bolg sailed to the land of Gallowna. They went to recoup their strength. Geali Dianvir was then sent back. He had to repair the damage to his people's reputation. He arrived in Bantry, in western County Cork. This lay in the province of Munster. He found the Fomorian queen surrounded by Balor's men. They applied venom to their swords each night. The venom came from a well. Warriors plunged their weapons into it. Geali Dianvir poured twenty measures of milk into the well. The milk came from the magic cow of abundance, the Glas Ghaibhleann. The poisoned water turned clear. He drove Balor's men to the outer reaches of the land.

okr.objective: Describe Geali Dianvir as the Fir Bolg hero who countered Balor's venom.
key_results: Geali Dianvir was the eldest son of the king of the Fir Bolg.
He returned from Gallowna to restore his people's reputation.
He turned the venom well to clear water with the cow of abundance.
